Options.Name: Hooks
Options.Doc: Function hooks for MemoryMgr. Must be a pointer to an instance of AkMemoryMgrHooks. See documentation for AkMemoryMgrHooks for details.

Options.Name: DebugLevel
Options.Doc: Memory debugging level. 0 = disabled. A value of 1 tracks memory allocations to identify memory leaks. A value of 2 activates memory stomp detection. A value of 3 enables both memory leak tracking and stomp detection.

Options.Name: StompDebugMemIDMask
Options.Doc: Bitmask indicating which AkMemID allocation should go through the stomp allocator. Defaults to all MemIDs.

Namespaces.Name: TempAlloc
Namespaces.Doc: Options for the TempAlloc sub-module of MemoryMgr.

Options.Name: MinimumBlockCount
Options.Doc: The number of blocks of memory the system is initialized with and is the minimum kept around forever. Higher values increase upfront memory use, but can reduce, or eliminate, the creation and destruction of memory blocks over time.

Options.Name: MinimumBlockSize
Options.Doc: The minimum size of each block. If a new allocation requests a new block of memory, then the new block is the size of the requested allocation times four, and then rounded up to the next multiple of this value. Defaults to 512 KiB.

Options.Name: MaximumUnusedBlocks
Options.Doc: The maximum number of blocks that the system keeps in an unused state, and avoids freeing. Higher values do not increase the peak memory use, but do prevent unused memory from being freed, in order to reduce creation and destruction of memory blocks.

Options.Name: EnableDebugDetailedStats
Options.Doc: Track detailed stats and include them in the detailed stat dump. Detailed stats include the size and quantity of each type of allocation from the system.

Options.Name: EnableDebugClearMemory
Options.Doc: Enable to clear any allocation to a deterministic garbage value. Useful to make sure memory is initialized properly.

Options.Name: EnableDebugSentinels
Options.Doc: Enable to write out sentinels between most allocations to help detect memory overwrites, verified at the end of a tick. Increases memory usage of blocks slightly.

Options.Name: EnableDebugFlushBlocks
Options.Doc: Enable to forcefully release all blocks at the end of a tick and recreate them from scratch every tick. Useful to ensure stale memory is not being accessed. This might interfere with some stats reporting due to blocks being released between ticks.

Options.Name: EnableDebugStandaloneAllocs
Options.Doc: Force the block size to be as small as possible for each allocation (smaller than can be achieved by just setting uMinimumBlockSize to very low values). Useful to investigate memory overruns in-depth, especially in conjunction with other options like bDebugFlushBlocks and the MemoryMgr's stomp allocator. If enabled, bDebugDetailedStats and bDebugEnableSentinels will be disabled. Greatly increases CPU and memory usage.

Namespaces.Name: BookmarkAlloc
Namespaces.Doc: Options for the BookmarkAlloc sub-module of MemoryMgr.

Options.Name: MinimumBlockCount
Options.Doc: The number of blocks of memory the system is initialized with and is the minimum kept around forever. Defaults to 1. Higher values increase upfront memory use, but can reduce, or eliminate, the creation and destruction of memory blocks over time.

Options.Name: MinimumBlockSize
Options.Doc: The minimum size of each block. If a new allocation requests a new block of memory, then the new block is the size of the requested allocation times four, and then rounded up to the next multiple of this value. Defaults to 128 KiB.

Options.Name: MaximumUnusedBlocks
Options.Doc: The maximum number of blocks that the system keeps in an unused state, and avoids freeing. Defaults to 1. Higher values do not increase the peak memory use, but do prevent unused memory from being freed, in order to reduce creation and destruction of memory blocks.

Options.Name: DebugDetailedStats
Options.Doc: Track detailed stats, specifically collection of Stats::uRecentPeakMemUsed. Enabled by default.

Options.Name: DebugClearMemory
Options.Doc: Clear any allocation to a deterministic garbage value during allocs, and after the stack is rewound to a bookmark. Useful to make sure memory is initialized properly.

Options.Name: DebugEnableSentinels
Options.Doc: Write out sentinels between most allocations to help detect memory overwrites, which are verified at the termination of a bookmark alloc region. Increases memory usage of blocks slightly.

Options.Name: DebugStandaloneAllocs
Options.Doc: Force the block size to be as small as possible for each allocation (smaller than can be achieved by just setting uMinimumBlockSize to very low values). Useful to investigate memory overruns in-depth, especially in conjunction with the MemoryMgr's stomp allocator. If enabled, bDebugEnableSentinels will be disabled. Greatly increases CPU and memory usage.

Namespaces.Name: MemoryArena_Primary
Namespaces.Doc: Options for the MemoryArena responsible for generic allocations within the Sound Engine.

Options.Name: Hooks
Options.Doc: Function hooks for this MemoryArena. Must be a pointer to an instance of AkMemoryArenaHooks. See documentation for AkMemoryArenaHooks for details.

Options.Name: EnableSba
Options.Doc: Used to determine if the SbaHeap should be initialized and utilized at all. If disabled, all small allocs (size < kAllocSizeMedium) will go into the TlsfHeap and be treated as Medium allocs.

Options.Name: SbaInitSize
Options.Doc: The size of the initial allocation of memory for the small block allocator (SBA). This allocation will be made inside the main TLSF heap, and will always persist. Sub-allocations that fit in this range will have better fragmentation characteristics, and an overall reduction in memory overhead. This does not have to be a power-of-two.

Options.Name: SbaSpanSize
Options.Doc: The size of each span of memory for the SBA. Each span has a unique size class. Lower values can slightly increase the overhead of initializing SBA allocations, but can reduce overall memory reservation. This must be a power-of-two.

Options.Name: SbaMaximumUnusedSpans
Options.Doc: The maximum number of SBA spans that the system keeps in an unused state, and avoids freeing. Higher values do not increase the peak memory use, but do prevent unused memory from being freed, in order to reduce creation and destruction of SBA spans.

Options.Name: TlsfInitSize
Options.Doc: The size of the initial span of memory requested for the main TLSF heap. This span will always persist. (does not have to be a power-of-two).

Options.Name: TlsfSpanSize
Options.Doc: When a memory allocation cannot fit in the main TLSF heap, and is a medium-sized allocation, new spans requested will be a multiple of this size (does not have to be a power-of-two).

Options.Name: TlsfLargeSpanSize
Options.Doc: When a memory allocation cannot fit in the main TLSF heap, and is a large-sized allocation, new spans requested will be a multiple of this size (does not have to be a power-of-two).

Options.Name: TlsfSpanOverhead
Options.Doc: The amount of allocation overhead assumed for each span. When new spans for TLSF are requested, this is subtracted from the size of the requested span, after multiplying the requested size up by uPageSize.

Options.Name: TlsfMaximumUnusedMediumSpans
Options.Doc: The maximum number of Medium spans that the system keeps in an unused state, and avoids freeing. Higher values do not increase the peak memory use, but do prevent unused memory from being freed, in order to reduce creation and destruction of medium spans.

Options.Name: TlsfMaximumUnusedLargeSpans
Options.Doc: The maximum number of Large spans that the system keeps in an unused state, and avoids freeing. Higher values do not increase the peak memory use, but do prevent unused memory from being freed, in order to reduce creation and destruction of large spans.

Options.Name: AllocSizeLarge
Options.Doc: Defines the minimum size for an allocation to qualify as Large. Default to UINT_MAX, so that all large allocs are treated as Medium allocs. Large allocs go into best-fit searches, same as medium allocations, but will go to a separate list of secondary spans, distinct from Medium allocations.

Options.Name: AllocSizeHuge
Options.Doc: Defines the minimum size for an allocation to qualify as Huge. Huge allocs always go into standalone spans even if there is space available in an existing span.

Options.Name: MemReservedLimit
Options.Doc: The limit on how much memory will be reserved by this arena. If a request for to reserve more memory is made that would go over this limit, a nullptr is returned. If set to zero, no limit is in place.

Namespaces.Name: StreamMgr
Namespaces.Doc: Options that affect file I/O behavior.

Options.Name: LowLevelIOHook
Options.Doc: Low-level I/O implementation for primary streaming device. Must point to an instance of AK::StreamMgr::IAkLowLevelIOHook.

Options.Name: IOMemory
Options.Doc:
Pointer for I/O memory allocated by user.
Set this if you don't want memory to be allocated via AK::MemoryMgr::Malign().
When set, PoolAttributes are ignored.

Options.Name: IOMemorySize
Options.Doc: Size of memory for I/O (for automatic streams). It is passed directly to AK::MemoryMgr::Malign(), after having been rounded down to a multiple of Granularity.

Options.Name: IOMemoryAlignment
Options.Doc: I/O memory alignment. It is passed directly to AK::MemoryMgr::Malign(). When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select a suitable alignment value for the current platform.

Options.Name: MemAllocType
Options.Doc: Attributes for I/O memory. Here, specify the allocation type (AkMemType_Device, and so on). It is passed directly to AK::MemoryMgr::Malign().

Options.Name: Granularity
Options.Doc: I/O requests granularity (typical bytes/request).

Options.Name: AutoStreamTargetBufferLength
Options.Doc: Targeted automatic stream buffer length (ms). When a stream reaches that buffering, it stops being scheduled for I/O except if the scheduler is idle.

Options.Name: MaxLatencyMs
Options.Doc: Maximum streaming latency (in ms). Used to warm up media streams in advance of playback in latency-sensitive scenarios, such as music playback.

Options.Name: LookAheadRatio
Options.Doc: Multiplication factor for all streaming look-ahead heuristic values, for music streams.

Options.Name: MaxConcurrentIO
Options.Doc: Maximum number of transfers that can be sent simultaneously to the Low-Level I/O.

Options.Name: UseStreamCache
Options.Doc: If true, the device attempts to reuse I/O buffers that have already been streamed from disk. This is particularly useful when streaming small looping sounds. However, there is a small increase in CPU usage when allocating memory, and a slightly larger memory footprint in the StreamManager pool.

Options.Name: MaxPinnedCacheSize
Options.Doc: Maximum number of bytes that can be pinned using AK::SoundEngine::PinEventInStreamCache() or AK::IAkStreamMgr::PinFileInCache(). When set to -1, the cache size is unlimited.

Options.Name: EnablePackageFallback
Options.Doc:
Determines what happens when a file is not found in a package.

When true, the default low-level I/O implementation will fall back on searching the base path locations using the platform's native filesystem API.

When false, files will be searched in packages exclusively, with no fallback on base path locations.

This policy can be changed at runtime by calling AK::StreamMgr::SetPackageFallbackBehavior.

Options.Name: UseSubfoldering
Options.Doc:
Change the sub-foldering policy of the Low-Level I/O hook for searching files.
This setting should match the 'Create Sub-Folders for Generated Files' of the Wwise Project Settings.

Namespaces.Name: SoundEngine
Namespaces.Doc: Options that affect general Sound Engine behavior.

Options.Name: Hooks
Options.Doc: Function hooks for the Sound Engine. Must be a pointer to an instance of AkSoundEngineHooks. See documentation for AkSoundEngineHooks for details.

Options.Name: PluginPath
Options.Doc: When using DLLs for plugins, specify their path. Leave unspecified if DLLs are in the same folder as the game executable.

Options.Name: MaxNumPaths
Options.Doc: Maximum number of paths for positioning.

Options.Name: ContinuousPlaybackLookAheadMS
Options.Doc:
Number of milliseconds ahead when continuous containers should instantiate a new voice before which next sounds should start playing.

This look-ahead time allows I/O to occur, and is especially useful to reduce the latency of continuous containers with trigger rate or sample-accurate transitions. You should set this value slightly above the required time for an asynchronous I/O stream to return the first buffers of file data.

This value is rounded up to audio frame granularity. An audio frame duration is equal to NumSamplesPerFrame / SampleRate. For example, given an audio frame duration of 10.6ms (the default on most platforms), a ContinuousPlaybackLookAheadMS value of 40.0 will be rounded up to exactly 4 audio frames, or ~42.4ms.

Options.Name: FloorPlane
Options.Doc:
Define the orientation of the the floor plane with respect to the X,Y,Z axes, and which axes represent the side, front and up vectors as a basis for rotations in Wwise.
AkFloorPlane is used in to orient the Game Object 3D Viewer in Wwise, and in the transformation of geometry instances in Wwise Acoustics.

AllowedValues.Doc: The floor is oriented along the ZX-plane. The front vector points towards +Z, the up vector towards +Y, and the side vector towards +X.
The floor is oriented along the XY-plane. The front vector points towards +X, the up vector towards +Z, and the side vector towards +Y.
The floor is oriented along the YZ-plane. The front vector points towards +Y, the up vector towards +X, and the side vector towards +Z.

Options.Name: GameUnitsPerMeters
Options.Doc:
The number of game units in a meter.

This setting is used to adapt the size of elements in the Authoring's Game Object 3D Viewer and Audio Object 3D Viewer to meters.
This setting is also used to simulate real-world positioning of System Audio Objects, to improve the HRTF in some cases.
For example, if your game engine sends positions in centimeters, the value of GameUnitsPerMeters should be 100.

Options.Name: EnableThread
Options.Doc: Use a Wwise-owned thread for processing audio. If set to false, audio processing will occur only inside a call to AK::SoundEngine::RenderAudio().

Options.Name: NumSamplesPerFrame
Options.Doc: Number of samples per audio frame (256, 512, 1024, or 2048).

Options.Name: SampleRate
Options.Doc:
Sample rate of the audio pipeline.

A value of 0 will select the native sample rate of the system. Once selected, the sample rate cannot change without re-initializing the Sound Engine.

Options.Name: MultipleBuffering
Options.Doc: Number of audio buffers to produce before waiting for the hardware to consume them. 2 == double-buffered, defaults to 4.

Options.Name: CommandQueueSize
Options.Doc: Size of the command queue, in bytes.

Options.Name: DebugOutOfRangeLimit
Options.Doc: Debug setting: Only used when EnableDebugOutOfRangeCheck is true. This defines the maximum values samples can have. Normal audio must be contained within +1/-1. This limit should be set higher to allow temporary or short excursions out of range.

Options.Name: EnableDebugOutOfRangeCheck
Options.Doc: Debug setting: Enable checks for out-of-range (and NAN) floats in the processing code. This incurs a small performance hit, but can be enabled in most scenarios. Will print error messages in the log if invalid values are found at various point in the pipeline. Contact AK Support with the new error messages for more information.

Options.Name: EnableOfflineRendering
Options.Doc: When true, the Wwise processing pipeline is disconnected from actual audio output hardware. Instead, every call to AK::SoundEngine::RenderAudio processes exactly one buffer of audio. This audio can be captured to a file using AK::SoundEngine::StartOutputCapture.

Options.Name: MaxHardwareTimeoutMs
Options.Doc: Amount of milliseconds to wait for HW devices to trigger an audio interrupt. If there is no interrupt after that time, the sound engine will revert to silent mode and continue operating until the HW finally comes back.

Options.Name: EnableHwCodecLowLatencyMode
Options.Doc:
Use low latency mode for hardware-accelerated codecs. 

If true, decoding jobs are submitted at the beginning of the Wwise update and audio processing blocks until the decoding jobs are complete. This eliminates the latency caused by hardware decoding but can lead to voice starvation when too many hardware-accelerated voices are playing concurrently.

Namespaces.Name: BankMgr
Namespaces.Doc: Options to control the behavior for loading bank and media files.

Options.Name: EnableThread
Options.Doc: Use a Wwise-owned thread for loading sound banks. If set to false, bank-loading will occur only inside a call to AK::SoundEngine::ProcessBanks().

Options.Name: EnableManualGameSyncPreparation
Options.Doc: When true, AK::SoundEngine::PrepareGameSync must be called manually to prepare game syncs.

Options.Name: BankReadBufferSize
Options.Doc: The number of bytes read by the BankReader when new data needs to be loaded from disk during serialization. Increasing this trades memory usage for larger, but fewer, file-read events during bank loading.

Namespaces.Name: Output
Namespaces.Doc: Options that configure the behavior of the primary audio output device.

Options.Name: AudioDeviceShareset
Options.Doc:
Unique ID of a custom audio device to be used. Custom audio devices are defined in the Audio Device Shareset section of the Wwise project.
If you want to output normally through the output device defined on the Master Bus in your project, leave this field to its default value (AK_INVALID_UNIQUE_ID, or value 0).
Otherwise, you can use AK::SoundEngine::GetIDFromString to generate the ID from the name of the shareset in the Wwise Project.

Options.Name: DeviceID
Options.Doc: Device-specific identifier, when multiple devices of the same type are possible. When 0, Wwise chooses the default output device for the output type.

Options.Name: PanningRule
Options.Doc: Rule for 3D panning of signals routed to a stereo bus.

AllowedValues.Doc: Left and right positioned 60 degrees apart by default (by default - see AK::SoundEngine::GetSpeakerAngles())
Left and right positioned 180 degrees apart.

Options.Name: EnableAutoPanningRule
Options.Doc:
Let Wwise choose the appropriate panning rule based on audio output device.

When headphones are detected at the output, "Headphones" is selected. Otherwise, "Speakers" is selected. Set this to false to opt out of this feature.

Note that not all platforms support headphone detection.

Options.Name: ChannelConfig
Options.Doc:
Channel configuration for this output. 

Must be the serialized value of an AkChannelConfig object. Call AkChannelConfig::Serialize on a valid AkChannelConfig instance to obtain this value.

Leave at 0 to let Wwise choose the appropriate channel configuration for the hardware.

Note that not all hardware support all configurations.

Options.Name: MaxSystemAudioObjects
Options.Doc:
Maximum number of System Audio Objects allowed for 3D Audio output.

This only applies to platforms that support 3D Audio. Dictates the maximum number of system resources to pre-allocate for System Audio Objects.

Set to 0 to disable the use of System Audio Objects.

Options.Name: EnableVerboseSystemLog
Options.Doc:
Print additional information about platform-specific audio output configuration to the system log.

Can be useful for debugging audio issues with specific hardware. Not all platforms support this option.

Namespaces.Name: JobMgr
Namespaces.Doc: Options to configure the Job Manager submodule for multicore processing of the Sound Engine.

Options.Name: MaxActiveWorkers_Generic
Options.Doc: The maximum number of concurrent workers that will be requested for general-purpose jobs. Must be >= 1.

Options.Name: MaxActiveWorkers_AudioProcessing
Options.Doc: The maximum number of concurrent workers that will be requested for jobs that process audio. Must be >= 1.

Options.Name: MaxActiveWorkers_Acoustics
Options.Doc: The maximum number of concurrent workers that will be requested for jobs that process Wwise Acoustics simulation. Must be >= 1.

Options.Name: NumMemorySlabs
Options.Doc: Number of memory slabs to pre-allocate for job manager memory. At least one slab per worker thread should be pre-allocated.

Options.Name: MemorySlabSize
Options.Doc: Size in bytes of each memory slab used for job manager memory. Must be a power of two.

Options.Name: EnableWorkerThreads
Options.Doc:
Let the Sound Engine manage a thread pool for each job type.

When this is enabled, the Sound Engine creates and manages a number of threads for each job type and automatically dispatches jobs to these threads. Enable this option if you want to take advantage of parallel processing in Wwise without the need to provide a custom implementation via AkSoundEngineHooks::pfRequestJobWorker. 

The number of threads created for each job type is dictated by the `NumWorkerThreads` runtime option.

Options.Name: NumWorkerThreads
Options.Doc: Size of the worker thread pool.

Options.Name: WorkerThreadExecutionTime
Options.Doc:
Maximum amount of time allotted for one execution of a worker, in microseconds.

Past this deadline, the worker stops consuming new jobs and the worker thread goes back to sleep.

A value of 0 means there is no limit, and the thread will keep working until there are no more jobs for it to work on.

This runtime option only applies to threads managed by the Sound Engine (see EnableWorkerThreads option).

Options.Name: WorkerThreadProperties
Options.Doc:
Pointer to an array of AkThreadProperties objects. The number of objects in the array must be equal to `NumWorkerThreads`.

When this option is set, the `JobWorker` options in AkOption_Threads are ignored.

Namespaces.Name: Acoustics
Namespaces.Doc: Options to configure the Wwise Acoustics submodule for realistic acoustic simulation.

Options.Name: Enable
Options.Doc:
Enable Wwise Acoustics feature.

When this is set to true, Wwise Acoustics is initialized as part of Sound Engine initialization.

Options.Name: MaxSoundPropagationDepth
Options.Doc:
Maximum number of rooms that sound can propagate through.

Must be less than or equal to the default value (8). Values below 2 will not propagate sound past the listener's own room.

Options.Name: MovementThreshold
Options.Doc:
Amount that an emitter or listener has to move to trigger a validation of reflections/diffraction. 

Larger values can reduce the CPU load at the cost of reduced accuracy. Note that the ray tracing itself is not affected by this value. Rays are cast each time a Wwise Acoustics update is executed.

Options.Name: NumberOfPrimaryRays
Options.Doc:
The number of primary rays used in the ray tracing engine.

A larger number of rays will increase the chances of finding reflection and diffraction paths, but will result in higher CPU usage.

Options.Name: MaxReflectionOrder
Options.Doc:
The number of bounces in a reflection path.

Must be in the range [1, 4]. A high reflection order renders more details at the expense of higher CPU usage.

Options.Name: MaxDiffractionOrder
Options.Doc:
The number of bends in a diffraction path.

Must be in the range [1, 8]. A high diffraction order accommodates more complex geometry at the expense of higher CPU usage.
Diffraction must be enabled on the geometry to find diffraction paths (see AkGeometryParams). Set to 0 to disable diffraction on all geometry.
This parameter limits the recursion depth of diffraction rays cast from the listener to scan the environment, and also the depth of the diffraction search to find paths between emitter and listener.
To optimize CPU usage, set it to the maximum number of edges you expect the obstructing geometry to traverse. 
For example, if box-shaped geometry is used exclusively, and only a single box is expected between an emitter and then listener, limiting MaxDiffractionOrder to 2 may be sufficient.
A diffraction path search starts from the listener, so when the maximum diffraction order is exceeded, the remaining geometry between the end of the path and the emitter is ignored.
In such case, where the search is terminated before reaching the emitter, the diffraction coefficient will be underestimated. It is calculated from a partial path, ignoring any remaining geometry.

Options.Name: MaxDiffractionPaths
Options.Doc:
Limit the maximum number of diffraction paths computed per emitter, excluding the direct/transmission path.

The acoustics engine searches for up to MaxDiffractionPaths paths and stops searching when this limit is reached.
Setting a low number for MaxDiffractionPaths (1-4) uses fewer CPU resources, but is more likely to cause discontinuities in the resulting audio. This can occur, for example, when a more prominent path is discovered, displacing a less prominent one.
Conversely, a larger number (8 or more) produces higher quality output but requires more CPU resources. The recommended range is 2-8.

Options.Name: MaxGlobalReflectionPaths
Options.Doc:
Global reflection path limit among all sound emitters with early reflections enabled.

Potential reflection paths, discovered by raycasting, are first sorted according to a heuristic to determine which paths are the most prominent. 
Afterwards, the full reflection path calculation is performed on only the MaxGlobalReflectionPaths, most prominent paths. Limiting the total number of reflection path calculations can significantly reduce CPU usage. Recommended range: 10-50. Range: [1, infinity[.

Options.Name: MaxEmitterRoomAuxSends
Options.Doc:
The maximum number of game-defined auxiliary sends that can originate from a single emitter.

An emitter can send to its own room, and to all adjacent rooms if the emitter and listener are in the same room. If a limit is set, the most prominent sends are kept, based on spread to the adjacent portal from the emitters perspective.
Set to 1 to only allow emitters to send directly to their current room, and to the room a listener is transitioning to if inside a portal. Set to 0 to disable the limit.

Options.Name: DiffractionOnReflectionsOrder
Options.Doc:
The maximum possible number of diffraction points at each end of a reflection path.

Diffraction on reflection allows reflections to fade in and out smoothly as the listener or emitter moves in and out of the reflection's shadow zone.
When greater than zero, diffraction rays are sent from the listener to search for reflections around one or more corners from the listener.
Diffraction must be enabled on the geometry to find diffracted reflections (see AkGeometryParams). Set to 0 to disable diffraction on reflections.
To allow reflections to propagate through portals without being cut off, set DiffractionOnReflectionsOrder to 2 or greater.

Options.Name: MaxDiffractionAngleDegrees
Options.Doc:
The largest possible diffraction value, in degrees, beyond which paths are not computed and are inaudible. 

Must be greater than zero.
A large value (for example, 360 degrees) allows paths to propagate further around corners and obstacles, but takes more CPU time to compute.
A gain is applied to each diffraction path to taper the volume of the path to zero as the diffraction angle approaches fMaxDiffractionAngleDegrees,
and appears in the Voice Inspector as 'Diffraction Tapering'. This tapering gain is applied in addition to the diffraction curves, and prevents paths from popping in or out suddenly when the maximum diffraction angle is exceeded.
In Wwise Authoring, the horizontal axis of a diffraction curve in the attenuation editor is defined over the range 0-100%, corresponding to angles 0-180 degrees.
If MaxDiffractionAngleDegrees is greater than 180 degrees, diffraction coefficients over 100% are clamped and the curve is evaluated at the rightmost point.

Options.Name: MaxPathLength
Options.Doc:
Upper limit of the total length of a path composed of a sequence of segments (or rays).

High values compute longer paths but increase the CPU cost.
Each individual sound is also affected by its maximum attenuation distance, specified in the Authoring tool. Reflection or diffraction paths, calculated inside Wwise Acoustics, will never exceed a sound's maximum attenuation distance.
Note, however, that attenuation is considered infinite if the furthest point is above the audibility threshold.

Options.Name: CPULimitPercentage
Options.Doc:
Defines the targeted max computation time allocated for Wwise Acoustics.

Defined as a percentage [0, 100] of the current audio frame. When the value is different from 0, Wwise Acoustics adapts dynamically the load balancing spread value between 1 and the specified LoadBalancingSpread according to current CPU usage and the specified CPU limit. Set to 0 to disable the dynamic load balancing spread computation.

Options.Name: LoadBalancingSpread
Options.Doc:
Spread the computation of paths on uLoadBalancingSpread frames [1..[.

When LoadBalancingSpread is set to 1, no load balancing is done. Values greater than 1 indicate the computation of paths will be spread on this number of frames. When CPU limit is active (see CPULimitPercentage), this setting represents the upper bound spread used by the dynamic load balancing instead of a fixed value.

Options.Name: SmoothingConstantMs
Options.Doc:
Enable parameter smoothing on the diffraction paths output from the Acoustics Engine.

Set SmoothingConstantMs to a value greater than 0 to define the time constant (in milliseconds) for parameter smoothing.
The time constant of an exponential moving average is the amount of time for the smoothed response of a unit step function to reach 1 - 1/e ~= 63.2% of the original signal.
A large value (eg. 500-1000 ms) results in less variance but introduces lag, which is a good choice when using conservative values for NumberOfPrimaryRays (eg. 5-10), MaxDiffractionPaths (eg. 1-3) or MovementThreshold ( > 1m ), in order to reduce overall CPU cost.
A small value (eg. 10-100 ms) results in greater accuracy and faster convergence of rendering parameters. Set to 0 to disable path smoothing.

Options.Name: AdjacentRoomBleed
Options.Doc:
Set a global scaling factor that manipulates reverb send values.

AdjacentRoomBleed affects the proportion of audio sent to adjacent rooms and to the emitter's current room.
This value is multiplied by AkPortalParams::AdjacentRoomBleed, which is used to scale reverb bleed for individual portals.
When calculating reverb send amounts, each portal's aperture is multiplied by AdjacentRoomBleed, which alters its perceived size:
- 1.0 (default): Maintains portals at their true geometric sizes (no scaling).
- > 1.0: Increases the perceived size of all portals, which increases bleed into adjacent rooms.
- < 1.0: Decreases the perceived size of all portals, which reduces bleed into adjacent rooms.
Valid range: (0.0 - infinity)
Note: Values close to 0 might cause abrupt portal transitions.

Options.Name: EnableGeometricDiffractionAndTransmission
Options.Doc: Enable computation of geometric diffraction and transmission paths for all sources that have the Enable Diffraction and Transmission box checked in the Positioning tab of the Wwise Property Editor. This flag enables sound paths around (diffraction) and through (transmission) geometry (see AK::Acoustics::SetGeometry). Setting EnableGeometricDiffractionAndTransmission to false implies that geometry is only to be used for reflection calculation. Diffraction edges must be enabled on geometry for diffraction calculation (see AkGeometryParams). If EnableGeometricDiffractionAndTransmission is false but a sound has Enable Diffraction and Transmission selected in the Positioning tab of the authoring tool, the sound will diffract through portals but will pass through geometry as if it is not there. One would typically disable this setting in the case that the game intends to perform its own obstruction calculation, but geometry is still passed to Wwise Acoustics for reflection calculation.

Options.Name: CalcEmitterVirtualPosition
Options.Doc: An emitter that is diffracted through a portal or around geometry will have its apparent or virtual position calculated by Wwise Acoustics and passed on to the sound engine.

Options.Name: TransmissionOperation
Options.Doc: The operation used to determine transmission loss on direct paths.

AllowedValues.Doc: Transmission loss of each hit surface is summed until it reaches 100%.

The inverse of transmission loss (1 - TL) is multiplied in succession, and the result inverted. With each hit surface, the effect of additional transmission loss is reduced. The total loss will approach but never reach 100% unless a surface with 100% loss is found.
The highest transmission loss of all hit surfaces is used.

Options.Name: ClusteringMinPoints
Options.Doc:
Minimum number of emitters in a cluster. 

Values less than 2 disable the clustering.
Note: Emitters with multi-positions are not clustered and are treated as independant emitters.
Note: Changing an emitter from single to multi-positions with load balancing enabled (see LoadBalancingSpread) might lead to unknown behaviors for a few frames.

Options.Name: ClusteringMaxDistance
Options.Doc: Max distance between emitters to be considered as neighbors. This distance is specified for the reference distance defined by ClusteringDeadZoneDistance.

Options.Name: ClusteringDeadZoneDistance
Options.Doc: Defines a dead zone around the listener where no emitters are clusters.

Options.Name: ReflectionPathSearchEffort
Options.Doc: Balances the reflection engine quality vs CPU performance. A low value indicates faster processing but less accurate reflections. A high value indicates lower CPU performance but more accurate reflections. Range: 0-1.

Options.Name: DiffractionFieldNodeBudget
Options.Doc:
Per-frame node expansion budget for the Diffraction Field (experimental).

Set to 0 (default) to disable the Diffraction Field; the per-emitter A* search is used instead.
Set to N > 0 to enable the field and allow up to N search graph nodes to be expanded per audio frame.
Portal diffraction fields use half this budget (N / 2) each.
Higher values converge the field faster after a listener move, at proportionally higher CPU cost per frame.
Tune based on scene edge density and MaxDiffractionOrder. See AkAcousticsInitSettings::uDiffractionFieldNodeBudget for details.
EnableGeometricDiffractionAndTransmission must also be true for any geometric diffraction to occur.

Options.Name: MaxRoomPropagationDistance
Options.Doc:
Maximum distance in game units that sound can propagate through Portals. (Experimental)

Rooms beyond this distance are culled, saving CPU usage.
Sounds will not propagate through a Portal if the shortest path to the listener from that portal would exceed this limit.
If the distance between the Listener and the bounds of a Room, in a straight line, exceeds this limit, that Room will not emit any sound or create sends to other Rooms.
This has no impact on Room Game Object registration. Culled Rooms are visible in the Game Object 3D Viewer when the Culled Rooms option is enabled.
The recommended starting point is to set this to match the longest attenuation distance for sounds expected to propagate through Rooms and Portals.

A value of 0 disables the limit.

Namespaces.Name: Profiler
Namespaces.Doc: Options to configure the Wwise Profiler.

Options.Name: Hooks
Options.Doc: Hooks for the CPU profiler. Must be a pointer to an AkProfilerHooks instance.

Options.Name: MonitorQueuePoolSize
Options.Doc: Size of the monitoring queue, in bytes. This parameter is not used in Release build.

Options.Name: CPUMonitorQueueMaxSize
Options.Doc: Maximum size of the CPU monitoring queue, per thread, in bytes. This parameter is not used in Release build.

Options.Name: Enable
Options.Doc:
Initialize the AK::Comm module as part of AK::SoundEngine::Init.

When set to false, the AK::Comm module is not initialized and it is not possible for Wwise Authoring to connect to the runtime.

This option applies to Debug and Profile configurations only. In the Release configuration, AK::Comm is always disabled.

AK::Comm is an optional submodule. Failure to initialize AK::Comm will not fail AK::SoundEngine::Init. Clients can check whether AK::Comm successfully initialized by calling AK::Comm::IsInitialized.

Options.Name: DiscoveryPort
Options.Doc: Port to listen for Game Discovery broadcast messages from the authoring application to discover games running on the network.

Options.Name: CommandPort
Options.Doc: Port used by Wwise Profiler to exchange data with connected Authoring application. Set to 0 to request a dynamic/ephemeral port.

Options.Name: API
Options.Doc: Which API to prefer for Wwise Profiler communications.

AllowedValues.Doc: Use the platform's default API for TCP/IP communication.

Options.Name: EnableSystemCommsManagement
Options.Doc:
Whether the operating system's communication library should be initialized and terminated alongside the sound engine.

If set to false, the game should load/initialize the console's communication library prior to calling this function.
Set to false only if your game already uses sockets outside the lifetime of the sound engine.

Options.Name: AppNetworkName
Options.Doc: Optional name that will be displayed over network remote connection of Wwise. Maximum 64 characters.

Options.Name: ProxyServerUrl
Options.Doc: Optional URL of Comm proxy server (only applicable for platforms incapable of acting as raw UDP/TCP servers). Maximum 128 characters.

Namespaces.Name: Threads
Namespaces.Doc: Options for configuring the threads managed by Wwise.

Options.Name: PrimaryStreamDevice_Priority
Options.Doc:
Priority of PrimaryStreamDevice thread. Range of values depends on platform. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select an appropriate priority for the current platform.

The PrimaryStreamDevice thread is used by the StreamMgr's primary device to process I/O requests.

Options.Name: PrimaryStreamDevice_StackSize
Options.Doc:
Stack size of PrimaryStreamDevice thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate stack size for the current platform.

The PrimaryStreamDevice thread is used by the StreamMgr's primary device to process I/O requests.

Options.Name: PrimaryStreamDevice_AffinityMask
Options.Doc: Core affinity for PrimaryStreamDevice thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate affinity mask for the current platform.

Options.Name: AudioMgr_Priority
Options.Doc:
Priority of AudioMgr thread. Range of values depends on platform. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select an appropriate priority for the current platform.

The AudioMgr thread is used by the AudioMgr to process commands and produce audio.

Options.Name: AudioMgr_StackSize
Options.Doc:
Stack size of AudioMgr thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate stack size for the current platform.

The AudioMgr thread is used by the AudioMgr to process commands and produce audio.

Options.Name: AudioMgr_AffinityMask
Options.Doc: Core affinity for AudioMgr thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate affinity mask for the current platform.

Options.Name: Suspend_Priority
Options.Doc:
Priority of Suspend thread. Range of values depends on platform. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select an appropriate priority for the current platform.

The AudioMgr thread keeps the Sound Engine rendering when suspended.

Options.Name: Suspend_StackSize
Options.Doc:
Stack size of Suspend thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate stack size for the current platform.

The AudioMgr thread keeps the Sound Engine rendering when suspended.

Options.Name: Suspend_AffinityMask
Options.Doc: Core affinity for Suspend thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate affinity mask for the current platform.

Options.Name: BankMgr_Priority
Options.Doc:
Priority of BankMgr thread. Range of values depends on platform. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select an appropriate priority for the current platform.

The BankMgr thread processes all bank and media operation.

Options.Name: BankMgr_StackSize
Options.Doc:
Stack size of BankMgr thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate stack size for the current platform.

The BankMgr thread processes all bank and media operation.

Options.Name: BankMgr_AffinityMask
Options.Doc: Core affinity for BankMgr thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate affinity mask for the current platform.

Options.Name: Profiler_Priority
Options.Doc:
Priority of Profiler thread. Range of values depends on platform. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select an appropriate priority for the current platform.

The Profiler thread processes network communications: executing live-edit actions from Authoring and sending back profiling data.

Options.Name: Profiler_StackSize
Options.Doc:
Stack size of Profiler thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate stack size for the current platform.

The Profiler thread processes network communications: executing live-edit actions from Authoring and sending back profiling data.

Options.Name: Profiler_AffinityMask
Options.Doc: Core affinity for Profiler thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate affinity mask for the current platform.

Options.Name: JobWorker_Priority
Options.Doc:
Priority of JobWorker thread. Range of values depends on platform. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically select an appropriate priority for the current platform.

The JobWorker thread pool processes chunks of work during audio rendering in a parallel fashion. The number of threads in the pool is specified by AkOption_JobMgr_NumWorkerThreads

Using these options, all JobWorker threads share the same thread properties. For finer control over priority and core affinity of individual threads in the pool, use AkOption_JobMgr_WorkerThreadProperties.

Options.Name: JobWorker_StackSize
Options.Doc:
Stack size of JobWorker thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate stack size for the current platform.

The JobWorker thread pool processes chunks of work during audio rendering in a parallel fashion. The number of threads in the pool is specified by AkOption_JobMgr_NumWorkerThreads

Using these options, all JobWorker threads share the same thread properties. For finer control over priority and core affinity of individual threads in the pool, use AkOption_JobMgr_WorkerThreadProperties.

Options.Name: JobWorker_AffinityMask
Options.Doc: Core affinity for JobWorker thread. When set to -1, Wwise will automatically determine an appropriate affinity mask for the current platform.
